result.topic_en: Gauss sketches a braid of four strands (a, b, c, d) and tabulates the changing complex coordinates of the strands at successive levels. He proposes describing the entanglement as an aggregate of parts, i.e. as the sequence of half-turns of one strand around another in a fixed sense of rotation, and includes a sketch of a curve winding around two points.

items.english: What matters is to represent the totality of the entanglement as an aggregate of parts in such a way that one sees which parts destroy (cancel) each other.
